summary: Yield = (2/pi) N tau / <tE> x detection efficiency from the E3 injection-recovery benchmark. Inputs are ranges, not measurements; the central column uses mid values.

scenarios.name: South ecliptic pole deep field (LMC direction, if overlapping)
North ecliptic pole deep field (high latitude)

caveats: Efficiency was measured on a bright (16 AB at 2 um), isolated synthetic source with 2% noise; real bulge photometry at 6.2 arcsec pixels is confusion-limited, so bulge/disk numbers are upper bounds. The most realistic near-term use is spectral blend decomposition of events already found by ground surveys (OGLE, MOA, KMTNet) that happen to fall in a SPHEREx visit. No event has been searched for or found in real SPHEREx data in this project. With the wide-survey cadence a 'detection' is a significant brightening during one visit; the timescale is then poorly constrained (E3: median |ln tE error| about 1, a factor ~2.7), so most such events could not be characterised from SPHEREx alone.
